==English==

===Etymology===
From {{m|en|you}} (as a determinative) + {{m|en|bastard}}.

===Pronunciation===
{{rfp|en}}

===Interjection===
{{en-intj}}

# {{lb|en|vulgar|offensive}} Used to insult the person addressed, expressing anger or contempt.
#* {{quote-av|en|year=1997|title=South Park|passage=“Oh my God, they killed Kenny!” “'''You bastards'''!”}}

====Usage notes====
* The phrase is an exclamatory noun phrase used as an utterance on its own. Such phrases never occupy a complement position in ordinary clause structure, so one can't say *''You bastard are late'' (compare ''Huddleston & Pullum 2002'', p. 353 note 14).
* ''You'' here is a determinative, not the head, as with other derogatory terms of address (''you stupid bastard''; ''Huddleston & Pullum 2002'', p. 523). The noun can therefore be modified (''you stupid bastard'', ''you sick bastard'') and can be singular, though ''you'' as a determinative otherwise takes a plural head.
* The bare noun is used in the same way (''Bastard!''). Other nouns that can fill the frame ''You X!'', such as ''idiot'', ''traitor'' and ''son of a bitch'', are terms of name-calling (''Ljung 2011'', pp. 126–128).
* Among friends the phrase can be affectionate (compare sense 4 of {{l|en|bastard}}). ''Potts 2007'' (p. 177) cites the slogan "Here's To You, Ya Bastard!" from an advertisement.

====Synonyms====
* {{l|en|you son of a bitch}}
